title: SRE Weekly Update - 2026-10-03
content:
Summary:

This week focused on two customer-impacting incidents (see Incidents), SLO health during a high-traffic launch, and completing the KV-cache eviction runbook updates. On-call rotation ran smoothly; handoff notes and a couple of outstanding action items are below.

Highlights:
- Incident SRE-2021 (cache eviction) caused elevated 5xx rates for the hosted API between 2026-10-01 02:10 UTC and 2026-10-01 03:05 UTC for a subset of customers. Root cause: cascade from aggressive KV-cache eviction + underprovisioned warmup for new model shards.
- Incident SRE-2022 (regional networking flaps) caused degraded availability for the EU region for ~20 minutes on 2026-10-02 during a provider routing change; automatic failover worked but with elevated latencies.
- p99 API latency for text-generation stayed at 210ms this week (target 200ms). Error budget burn is ~12% across services for the trailing 7 days.
- Updated the KV-cache eviction runbook, added step-by-step rollback play, and added better alerting thresholds.

Incidents (short):

1) SRE-2021 - KV-cache eviction spike
- Timeline: 2026-10-01 02:08 UTC (first alert) - 2026-10-01 03:05 UTC (mitigated)
- Impact: 5xx rate spike in hosted API (5-12% for affected shard group), increased tail latency for affected tenants, some customer retries and elevated error reporting to CS.
- Detection: SLO alert (error-rate burn) triggered automatic page; multiple on-call members paged.
- Mitigation: Rolled back recent eviction tuning (reverted eviction aggressiveness flag), scaled up warm pool for model shards, applied temporary routing to healthy replicas.
- Root cause: regressed eviction config pushed in internal rollout combined with a warmup race when re-sharding under load.
- RCA status: Draft RCA linked (confluence). Short-term actions complete; longer-term mitigations below.

2) SRE-2022 - EU networking flap
- Timeline: 2026-10-02 11:41 UTC - 2026-10-02 12:02 UTC
- Impact: Elevated latency and partial request timeouts for EU region customers; global failover engaged for a fraction of traffic, causing higher latencies for routed requests.
- Detection: Provider outage alert + synthetic checks failing for EU edge.
- Mitigation: Manual failover to alternate peering, roll back recent BGP community change via provider portal.
- Root cause: Upstream provider BGP config change; our health checks and failover logic worked as designed but threshold tuning needs refinement to reduce unnecessary broad failovers.
- RCA status: Investigating provider timeline; updating failover threshold config is an action item.

SLO and Metrics:
- Target: API error rate < 0.5% (rolling 7d), p99 latency < 200ms for text generation.
- This week: 7d error rate = 0.64% (above target); p99 = 210ms.
- Error budget burn: ~12% over the last 7 days, with SRE-2021 accounting for most of the spike.
- Alerts we saw: error-rate paging at 0.5% threshold fired twice; on-call responded within SLA.

On-call handoffs / rotations:
- Primary on-call (this week): Lina Chen (owner) - reachable in #ops-oncall and phone.
- Secondary: Marcus Rao.
- Next-week primary: Priya Natarajan (rotation starts 2026-10-10 00:00 UTC).
- Handoff notes:
  - All on-call runbooks are in Confluence (see linked_artifacts).
  - Reminder: when tripping SLO error-rate alerts, check both KV-cache eviction metrics and index shard rebalances before escalating.
  - If network provider flaps observed, follow provider-flap checklist: verify peering, check BGP communities, activate manual peering failover if latencies > 2x baseline for >5 minutes.

Runbooks / Playbooks updated this week:
- KV-cache eviction runbook: added graduated rollback steps, safer default eviction thresholds, automated warm-pool scale-up.
- Failover threshold playbook: drafted - TODO to finalize alarms and automatic versus manual steps.

Operational changes & upcoming work:
- Deploying a change next week to introduce a 30s delay window before aggressive shard eviction when re-sharding. Target deploy: 2026-10-06 (canary -> gradual rollout). Owner: Omar Delgado.
- Failover threshold tuning: Priya to own tuning of per-region failover thresholds and synthetic check windows (action item).
- Capacity: request to increase warm-pool reserve on dedicated clusters by +10% for the next 30 days to reduce cold starts during bursts (finance escalation in progress).
- Observability: adding a p95/p99 histogram for KV-cache eviction durations to better correlate with 5xx spikes (instrumentation PR in review: GH #3421).

Action items (owners and eta):
- (Omar) Implement 30s eviction delay in canary (ETA: 2026-10-06) - IN_PROGRESS.
- (Priya) Finalize failover threshold playbook and update alerts (ETA: 2026-10-09) - TODO.
- (Marcus) Run a synthetic soak test for EU region peering failover to validate thresholds (ETA: 2026-10-08) - TODO.
- (Lina) Complete RCA doc for SRE-2021 and share with CS & product (ETA: 2026-10-05) - IN_PROGRESS.

Meeting notes (this week):
- Mon standup (2026-09-28): quick sync on rollout for eviction tuning; agreed to gate any further eviction parameter changes behind CI canary and expanded unit tests.
- Wed incident review (2026-10-02): post-incident recap for SRE-2021; agreed to immediate runbook updates and to add warm-pool alarms.
- Thu SLO review (2026-10-03): saw slight degradation in p99 latency; tracing shows increased tail caused by occasional shard cold starts. Decided to push warm-pool reserve change for peak hours only to limit cost impact.

Notes to self / informal items:
- Need to circle back with Product infra on whether model re-sharding cadence can be smoothed out during low-traffic windows. Slack thread: #prod-modeling (link above).
- Consider a short explainer for CS that clarifies what customers will see during automatic failovers vs. regional outages.

Files and links (quick):
- Incident tickets: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-2021, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-2022
- RCA draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/kv-cache-eviction-RCA
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/KV+Cache+Eviction+Runbook
- Instrumentation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3421

If anything urgent comes up during the weekend, page primary on-call. Otherwise we'll revisit action items in next Monday's sync.

-- Lina
